answer: (1) Twitch: two integration styles — plain iframe `https://player.twitch.tv/?channel=<name>&parent=<domain>` or interactive script `https://player.twitch.tv/js/embed/v1.js` with `new Twitch.Player(divId, {channel, parent: [...], width, height})`; the combined player+chat uses `https://embed.twitch.tv/embed/v1.js` with `new Twitch.Embed(..., {layout: 'video-with-chat'})`. `parent` is required, one entry per embedding domain (repeat the query param), embedding pages must be HTTPS, min 400x300. `autoplay` defaults true, `muted` defaults false — for a 24/7 site use `muted=true&autoplay=true` since browsers block unmuted autoplay. On Vercel previews, compute `parent` at runtime from `window.location.hostname` (no wildcards). YouTube equivalent: iframe `https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEo_ID?autoplay=1&mute=1&playsinline=1&enablejsapi=1&origin=<your-origin>`; live-by-channel `embed/live_stream?channel=CHANNEL_ID` works but is undocumented — more robust is resolving the live videoId server-side (Data API) and embedding it. Make the switch a config union: `{provider:'twitch',channel}|{provider:'youtube',videoId|channelId}` rendered by one client component. (2) No Vercel constraint on client-side WebSockets: the browser connects directly to `wss://<ref>.supabase.co/realtime/v1/websocket` and never traverses Vercel. The old serverless limitation applied only to functions holding sockets — and even that is now lifted: Vercel Functions serve WebSockets under Fluid compute (default since 2025-04-23), closing at max duration. You don't need it; let Supabase hold the socket. (3) `import { ImageResponse } from 'next/og'` — `new ImageResponse(element, {width=1200, height=630, fonts, emoji='twemoji', debug, status, headers})`; use route handlers or `opengraph-image.tsx`. Satori limits: flexbox only (no grid), ttf/otf/woff fonts (no woff2), 500KB total bundle, Node.js runtime supported. (4) `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined at build time and frozen; server-only vars stay in Node. Vercel scopes values per environment (Production/Preview/Development, plus per-branch preview overrides); changes require redeploy; preview builds bake preview values — so `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` can safely differ per environment. (5) Statically render the shell (layout + Suspense), fetch the initial snapshot in a dynamic server component (`export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` or default-uncached fetch; note these segment configs are removed under Next 16 Cache Components), and let the client component take over via Realtime. Serve the dynamic data route with `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; shell/clip pages can use `s-maxage`/`stale-while-revalidate`. (6) Generate a bypass secret, then Playwright `use.extraHTTPHeaders: {'x-vercel-protection-bypass': process.env.VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET, 'x-vercel-set-bypass-cookie': 'true'}` (Vercel's own documented example).

facts.claim: Twitch requires embed users to verify where embeds are used via the `parent` parameter; domains using Twitch embeds must use SSL certificates; embeds have minimum size requirements

Twitch iframe player base URL is https://player.twitch.tv/ with `parent` required ("You must have one parent key for each domain your site uses"), content params channel/video/collection, `autoplay` (boolean, default true), `muted` (boolean, default false), `time`; interactive embed script is https://player.twitch.tv/js/embed/v1.js with `new Twitch.Player("<div id>", options)`, min 400x300, `parent` as array required when embedded cross-domain

Twitch 'everything' (video+chat) embed script is https://embed.twitch.tv/embed/v1.js using `new Twitch.Embed()` with options including `parent` (string array), `layout: "video-with-chat"`, `autoplay` (default true), `muted` (default false), `theme` ('light'|'dark'), defaults 940x480

Twitch parent values cannot carry a port; per a Twitch dev forum moderator, localhost/127.0.0.1 parents are assumed port 80 (HTTP) and other domains port 443, so dev servers on :3000 fail (forum guidance, not official docs)

YouTube embed URL is https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID; documented params include `autoplay` (0 default/1), `enablejsapi` (1 enables IFrame API control), `origin` (recommended with enablejsapi for security), `playsinline` (1 = inline on iOS), `controls`, `loop`; `modestbranding`/`showinfo` are deprecated and non-functional
The official player_parameters page does NOT document a dedicated `mute` parameter (mute appears only as the [m] keyboard control under `disablekb`)

Vercel Functions can serve WebSocket connections; a connection is pinned to one function instance; connections close when the function reaches its maximum duration; WebSockets require Fluid compute, the default for projects created on or after April 23, 2025; Next.js needs the experimental_upgradeWebSocket() API from @vercel/functions
Supabase Realtime transport is WebSocket: connection URL wss://<PROJECT_REF>.supabase.co/realtime/v1/websocket?apikey=<API_KEY> (browser connects directly to Supabase, not through Vercel)

ImageResponse is imported from 'next/og'; options: width (default 1200), height (default 630), emoji ('twemoji'|'blobmoji'|'noto'|'openmoji', default 'twemoji'), fonts [{name, data: ArrayBuffer, weight, style}], debug (default false), status (default 200), statusText, headers; moved from next/server to next/og in v14.0.0

ImageResponse/@vercel/og limits: Satori+Resvg render to PNG; only flexbox and a CSS subset (no display:grid); max 500KB bundle including JSX, CSS, fonts, images; only ttf/otf/woff fonts (ttf/otf preferred); supported on the Node.js runtime; recommended OG size 1200x630; usable in opengraph-image.tsx file convention with exported alt/size/contentType

NEXT_PUBLIC_ vars are inlined at build time into the JS bundle and frozen after build ("After being built, your app will no longer respond to changes to these environment variables"); dynamic lookups like process.env[varName] are NOT inlined; non-prefixed vars are server-only; load order: process.env, .env.$(NODE_ENV).local, .env.local, .env.$(NODE_ENV), .env

Vercel env vars are scoped to Production, Preview (with per-branch overrides that take precedence), Development (pulled via `vercel env pull`), and custom environments; changes apply only to new deployments; total limit 64KB per deployment (5KB per var on edge runtime)

In the non-Cache-Components model: `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` forces per-request rendering (equivalent to fetch {cache:'no-store', next:{revalidate:0}}); `export const revalidate = 0` makes a page always dynamically rendered; fetch requests are NOT cached by default; revalidate value must be statically analyzable
In Next.js v16.0.0, the `dynamic`, `dynamicParams`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` route segment configs are removed when Cache Components (cacheComponents flag) is enabled

Vercel default cache header is `cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` (no caching); `s-maxage` and `stale-while-revalidate` are consumed by Vercel's CDN and stripped from client responses; header priority: Vercel-CDN-Cache-Control > CDN-Cache-Control > Cache-Control; use `private`/`no-store` for real-time or per-user data; SWR pattern example `Cache-Control: s-maxage=1, stale-while-revalidate=59`

Protection Bypass for Automation: authenticate with header or query param `x-vercel-protection-bypass: <secret>`; secret auto-set as system env var VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET; `x-vercel-set-bypass-cookie: true` (or `samesitenone` for iframes) sets a bypass cookie for follow-up in-browser requests; official Playwright example uses use.extraHTTPHeaders with both headers; bypasses Password Protection, Vercel Authentication, Trusted IPs, firewall blocks and bot challenges, but not active DDoS mitigations; regenerating the secret invalidates previous deployments until redeploy

gotchas: Twitch parent + Vercel previews: parent values are exact hostnames (no wildcards, no ports), and preview URLs change per deployment. Since the JS embed takes `parent` as a runtime option, pass `[window.location.hostname]` so the same code works on localhost, previews, and production. Twitch parent on localhost: forum moderators say only port 80/443 is assumed (localhost:3000 fails) — this contradicts scattered community reports that :3000 works; official docs are silent, so verify empirically or test on a deployed preview.

YouTube `mute=1` is used everywhere (including Google-adjacent examples and vercel/next.js issue #77447 for @next/third-parties) but is absent from the official player_parameters reference — sources disagree. It does work in practice; the officially documented path is enablejsapi + player.mute() via the IFrame API. Either way, unmuted autoplay is blocked by modern browsers, so always pair autoplay with mute.

The `https://www.youtube.com/embed/live_stream?channel=CHANNEL_ID` endpoint is not in Google's official developer docs; secondary sources also report live-stream embedding requires the channel to have embedding allowed, historically gated on monetization/AdSense linkage — viewers otherwise see 'Playback on other websites has been disabled'. Safer: resolve the current live videoId server-side and embed it as a normal video.

The old 'Vercel serverless functions can't hold WebSockets' rule is obsolete as of Fluid compute (docs updated 2026): functions CAN now serve WebSockets, but connections still die at maxDuration. Neither constraint ever applied to browser->Supabase connections, which bypass Vercel entirely.

NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are baked in at build time per deployment — a Preview build permanently contains Preview values; you cannot flip them at runtime, and dynamic process.env[name] lookups silently fail to inline (undefined in the browser). Point the stream-provider toggle at a runtime-fetched config (or Supabase row) if you want to switch Twitch/YouTube without redeploying; env vars alone require a redeploy to change.

Do NOT try to make the page itself 1-second-fresh via ISR (`revalidate: 1`) — every visitor triggers regeneration and data still lags; the correct split is cached static shell + no-store initial data + Supabase Realtime push. If you adopt Next 16 with cacheComponents enabled, `dynamic`/`revalidate`/`fetchCache` exports are gone and force-dynamic behavior comes from request-time APIs like connection() instead.
Vercel strips `s-maxage` and `stale-while-revalidate` before responses reach the browser — they only steer Vercel's CDN; use plain max-age/private/no-store for browser behavior.

Playwright + preview protection: when the embed/player runs in an iframe context, `x-vercel-set-bypass-cookie: true` sets a SameSite=Lax cookie which may not be sent — use value `samesitenone`. Also note the bypass secret is per-project and regenerating it invalidates all existing deployments until you redeploy.
Twitch embeds must not be visually obscured — Twitch may disable features (e.g., chat messaging) if the player is hidden or covered by overlays, relevant for a commentary-overlay site design.
unconfirmed: Whether Twitch's parent=localhost port-80/443 restriction still holds in 2026 — the claim comes from a Twitch dev forum moderator thread (2020-era), not current official docs; current official embed docs do not mention localhost at all.

The exact current requirements for YouTube live-stream embedding (monetization/AdSense linkage, 'enable embedding' toggle in live settings) — only secondary sources (EventMobi, SpatialChat, WebinarJam) found; the YouTube Help article at support.google.com/youtube/answer/2853700 no longer covers embedding.
The `youtube.com/embed/live_stream?channel=` URL's official status — it functions per many secondary sources but appears in no current Google developer documentation.

Plan availability of Vercel Protection Bypass for Automation (the docs page shows role requirements but no explicit plan/pricing gate; historically it was tied to plans with Deployment Protection features).
Whether the YouTube `mute` URL parameter is guaranteed stable — it works ubiquitously but is undocumented in the official player_parameters reference, so it could theoretically change without notice.

Precise minimum `revalidate` interval enforced by Vercel ISR (docs only say the value must be a statically analyzable number of seconds; per-second ISR was not explicitly documented as supported or bounded).
